name: Twenty
one_liner: Twenty is an open-source, self-hostable CRM with a customizable data model, REST and GraphQL APIs, workflows, AI agents and an apps framework for building a custom CRM.

auth.note: OAuth2 auth code+PKCE and client credentials; API keys for scripts

access.note: Free trial without credit card; paid plans from $9/user/month; self-host free

api_surface.note: Core and Metadata APIs in REST and GraphQL

mcp.note: Official MCP server with OAuth or API key auth

verdict.note: Free self-hosted plan and self-serve cloud plans

notes: API keys are generated in Settings; the OpenAPI spec says tokens come from Settings → Playground. Rate limit is 50 calls/min on Pro and 100 on Organization. Webhooks exist. Admin requirement for app installs is not shown.

name: Twilio
one_liner: Twilio is a cloud communications platform offering APIs for SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email, video, verification and customer data, plus AI conversation tooling for building agents.

auth.note: API keys are the preferred way to authenticate with REST APIs; Main key equals Account SID and Auth Token.

access.note: Free trial with no credit card required, then pay-as-you-go.

api_surface.note: Official server-side SDKs in multiple languages using Account SID and Auth Token.

mcp.note: Hosted Twilio MCP server at mcp.twilio.com/docs; public beta, read-only docs search.

notes: Official MCP is public beta and read-only (docs search/retrieve, no API execution, no credentials); execute-capable OAuth MCP tools are only planned. An older Twilio Alpha MCP server (npm/repo) did execute API calls with an API key. Basic auth is inferred from SID/token SDK usage.

name: Plain
one_liner: Plain is a customer support platform for B2B teams that unifies Slack, email and chat threads with customer context and built-in AI agents, exposing a full GraphQL API and an MCP server.

auth.note: Machine user API keys passed as Bearer; OAuth app for calling as a workspace user

access.note: Plans and free trial; Frontier needs sales

api_surface.note: Plain is built on the same GraphQL API; no UI/API limitations

mcp.note: Official MCP server at mcp.plain.com/mcp with ~400 tools

verdict.note: Self-created API keys with fine-grained permissions
API listed in developer platform features; no credit card trial

notes: API keys are created in Settings by a workspace user (permissions needed unclear). MCP uses OAuth only for the MCP server. The External Agents (bring your own agent) feature is listed under Frontier (sales). Pricing page feature matrix does not clearly show the API plan tier.

name: GoHighLevel
one_liner: GoHighLevel is an all-in-one CRM, marketing automation and agency platform with a REST API (contacts, conversations, calendars, payments, webhooks) and a developer Marketplace.

auth.note: OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens are the supported auth methods; legacy API keys are being phased out

access.note: 14-day free trial with full tier features; self-serve plans
API access across Starter, Unlimited and Founder plans

api_surface.note: REST API covering CRM, conversations, calendars, opportunities, payments, webhooks

mcp.note: No MCP server mentioned in the fetched official docs or developer pages

verdict.note: Documented REST API with self-serve credentials
PIT and OAuth available on all plans

notes: No MCP found in fetched pages (one may exist elsewhere). Trial including API credentials is inferred from the 14-day full-access trial plus API on all plans. Create Sub-Account and Enable SaaS endpoints need the Founder plan. API V1 is end-of-support. The Stoplight page was empty.

name: Sherlock
one_liner: Open-source Python CLI that hunts down social media accounts by username across 400+ social networks and saves the results to text, CSV or XLSX files.

auth.note: Local CLI; the README documents installation and usage with no credentials or API keys.

access.note: MIT-licensed; installable freely via pipx, Docker or dnf.

api_surface.note: CLI only, with flags for JSON/CSV/XLSX output, site filters, proxy and timeout. No hosted API is documented.

mcp.note: Third-party FastMCP server that wraps the Sherlock CLI and exposes a search_username tool.

verdict.note: A wrappable local CLI, so buildable now.

notes: Interpreted as the sherlock-project username-OSINT CLI. The other fetched pages (sherlock.xyz audit API, sherlock.sh, the sherlock locking library, sherlocksuite) are different products and were ignored. The MCP servers are community-only. Results depend on the site checks in the tool's data.json.

name: Datadog
one_liner: Datadog is a cloud observability and security platform (metrics, logs, traces, monitors, incidents) with a broad REST API, official client libraries and an official remote MCP server.

auth.note: API key and application key headers
All requests need API key; reads need application key

access.note: Pricing page with Start Free Trial; keys managed in org settings

api_surface.note: HTTP REST API with official client libraries, v1 and v2 endpoints

verdict.note: Documented REST API with key auth

notes: OAuth2 is documented for the MCP server only, not for the REST API, so it is not listed as an API auth method. Fixing auth_methods to api_key only is more accurate. A free trial is mentioned on the pricing page. Pup CLI also exists.

name: Linear
one_liner: Linear is a project and issue tracking tool for software teams, with a public GraphQL API, webhooks, a TypeScript SDK, an agent platform and an official hosted MCP server.

auth.note: API supports personal API keys and OAuth2
OAuth2 authorization code, PKCE and client credentials

access.note: Free plan at $0 includes API and webhook access
Personal API keys are created in Security & access settings

api_surface.note: GraphQL endpoint with queries and mutations for issues, teams and more
Docs index covering GraphQL, webhooks, attachments, customers, SDK and agents

mcp.note: Changelog announcing the official MCP server

verdict.note: API and MCP access included on the free plan

one_liner.note: Linear's public API is built using GraphQL

notes: Webhooks exist alongside the GraphQL API. The MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, and also accepts a bearer token or API key. OAuth app creation is workspace-based, and the docs recommend a dedicated workspace because each admin gets access. Some features, such as higher rate limits, depend on plan.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
one_liner: Amazon's Selling Partner API (SP-API) is a REST API that lets sellers and vendors programmatically access orders, listings, inventory, shipments, payments, reports and more.

auth.note: Public apps use OAuth 2.0 via Login with Amazon; private apps self-authorize.

access.note: A Professional selling account and a developer profile are needed, and Amazon evaluates the profile.

api_surface.note: Official docs for the REST-based SP-API, including SDKs and many API areas.

mcp.note: Selling Partner plugin in beta for AI assistants; no MCP server URL given.

verdict.note: Private seller apps are self-authorized and need a Professional selling account.

notes: Developer profile is reviewed by Amazon and may need extra info. Public apps must be listed in the Appstore and be authorized by sellers. Restricted data needs a Restricted Data Token. Amazon's own Selling Partner plugin is in beta, with no MCP URL; the MCP found is third-party (Kuudo).

name: Devin
one_liner: Devin is an autonomous AI software engineer from Cognition that writes, runs and tests code, with a v3 REST API and an official MCP server for managing sessions, playbooks, knowledge and schedules.

auth.note: Service user API keys and PATs with cog_ prefix as Bearer token; legacy keys deprecated

access.note: Teams is self-serve at $80/month and lists Devin API; Enterprise is contact sales
Teams quick start for standard organizations

api_surface.note: Organization and Enterprise API at api.devin.ai/v3 covering sessions, knowledge, playbooks, secrets

mcp.note: Official Devin MCP server at https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp

verdict.note: Documented token auth with self-serve service user provisioning
Self-serve paid Teams plan includes Devin API

notes: Service users are provisioned in Settings > Devin API, likely requiring org admin rights (not confirmed in pages). Enterprise API requires Enterprise plan. Legacy v1/v2 apk_ keys are deprecated. MCP supports the same API keys; OAuth appears only for MCP servers Devin CLI connects to.

name: Paygent Connect
one_liner: Paygent (paygent.to) is an SDK and backend REST API that meters per-user LLM costs and enforces spending limits for AI agents; this is the closest documented match, since no fetched page confirms 'Paygent Connect' itself.

auth.note: Bearer pg_live_ API key; POST /products mints the first key

api_surface.note: Small REST API for products, plans, users and subscriptions

mcp.note: No MCP server found on the docs home page

verdict.note: Self-serve key creation and documented REST API

notes: Identity is ambiguous. The fetched pages cover several unrelated 'Paygent' products (paygent.to, withpaygent.com, paygent.uk, gopaygent.com) plus NMI docs. None confirms 'Paygent Connect' or NMI-powered payments. This row describes paygent.to only. NMI has a docs-only MCP, not verified for Paygent.
